# origin iam and sts commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.20.1).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin iam` command, and the `origin sts` command that assumes a service account with an identity provider's token. Logging in is `origin id login`; see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md).

## origin iam

Identity and access management: role bindings, service accounts, roles, permissions, your user and the audit log. Role bindings, service accounts and the audit log are an organization's (`--organization`); roles, permissions and your user are the same in every organization. A role binding's member is `user:{email}` or `serviceAccount:{service_account}`; `origin iam list-role-bindings --organization -` lists the bindings you hold, in every organization.

Every `origin iam` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://iam.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_IAM_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-audit-log-entry

Returns an audit log entry. Needs `iam.audit_log.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-audit-log-entry [OPTIONS] --audit-log-entry <AUDIT_LOG_ENTRY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--audit-log-entry` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--audit-log-entry <AUDIT_LOG_ENTRY>` | yes | The entry to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/auditLogEntries/{audit_log_entry}`. |

### list-audit-log-entries

Lists an organization's audit log entries, most recent first, optionally only a project's, an actor's or an action's. Needs `iam.audit_log.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-audit-log-entries [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | Only the entries of changes limited to this project, `projects/{project}`. Every entry when empty. |
| `--actor <ACTOR>` | no | Only the entries of changes made by this member's account, `user:{email}` or `serviceAccount:{service_account}`. Every actor's when empty. |
| `--action <ACTION>` | no | Only the entries of this action, such as `iam.role.assign`. Every action's when empty. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most entries to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### get-federated-credential

Returns a federated credential, deleted or not. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The `{service_account}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>` | yes | The federated credential to return. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`. |

### list-federated-credentials

Lists a service account's federated credentials, oldest first. Deleted ones are listed only when `--show-deleted` is set. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-federated-credentials [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The `{service_account}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most federated credentials to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--show-deleted <true|false>` | no | Whether deleted federated credentials are listed too. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |

### create-federated-credential

Creates a federated credential on an active `WORKLOAD` service account. Anyone whose token matches it acts as the service account, so creating one needs `iam.service_account.create` and `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization: the right to act as the account yourself. Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` when a condition contains `*`, or when no condition names an identity that never changes: `repository_id` or `repository_owner_id` for GitHub Actions' issuer, `project_id` or `namespace_id` for GitLab.com's, `sub` for any other.

```sh
origin iam create-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME> --issuer <ISSUER> --condition <KEY=VALUE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The `{service_account}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | A name of your own, shown in the console; at most 100 characters. |
| `--issuer <ISSUER>` | yes | The identity provider whose tokens are trusted: a token's `iss`, matched exactly, an `https` URL that serves `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, such as `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. |
| `--audience <AUDIENCE>` | no | The audience a token must be issued for, its `aud`, matched exactly; `https://sts.origincloudapis.eu` when the create leaves it empty. |
| `--condition <KEY=VALUE>` | yes | The claims a token must carry, each with exactly this value, such as `repository_id` and `environment` for GitHub Actions. At least one, on an identity that never changes. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day returns the federated credential the first request created, as it is now, instead of creating a second. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT`. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-federated-credential

Deletes a federated credential: no token is exchanged for it from then on, and an access token already exchanged for it is refused on its next request. It stays readable as `DELETED`. Deleting a deleted one succeeds. Needs `iam.service_account.revoke` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam delete-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The `{service_account}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>` | yes | The federated credential to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-permission

Returns a permission.

```sh
origin iam get-permission [OPTIONS] --permission <PERMISSION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--permission <PERMISSION>` | yes | The permission to return, `permissions/{permission}`. Its id, or its whole name, `permissions/{permission}`. |

### list-permissions

Lists every permission the platform checks, in catalog order, including those no predefined role grants by default, such as the billing account permissions.

```sh
origin iam list-permissions [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### test-iam-permissions

Returns the subset of `--permission` the caller holds on an organization or a project. A permission held on the organization counts for each of its projects; one held on a project counts only there. Every resource in a project is governed by the project's permissions, so asking about the project answers for each of its resources. A permission the catalog doesn't name is never held.

```sh
origin iam test-iam-permissions [OPTIONS] --resource <RESOURCE> --permission <PERMISSION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | yes | The organization, `organizations/{organization}`, or the project, `projects/{project}`, to test the permissions on. |
| `--permission <PERMISSION>` | yes | The permissions to test, by their keys, such as `pvs.volume.create`; at most 100. Repeat for more. |

### get-role

Returns a role.

```sh
origin iam get-role [OPTIONS] --role <ROLE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--role <ROLE>` | yes | The role to return, `roles/{role}`. Its id, or its whole name, `roles/{role}`. |

### list-roles

Lists every predefined role, in catalog order.

```sh
origin iam list-roles [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-role-binding

Returns a role binding. Needs `iam.member.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-role-binding [OPTIONS] --role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--role-binding` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>` | yes | The binding to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`. |

### list-role-bindings

Lists an organization's role bindings, oldest first, optionally only a member's or a project's. Needs `iam.member.list` on the organization. With the parent `organizations/-` it lists the caller's own bindings in every organization and needs no permission; `--member` must be empty there.

```sh
origin iam list-role-bindings [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--member <MEMBER>` | no | Only the bindings of this member, `user:{email}` or `serviceAccount:{service_account}`. Every member's when empty. |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | Only the bindings limited to this project, `projects/{project}`. Every binding, organization-wide or not, when empty. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most bindings to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-role-binding

Grants a role to a member. Needs `iam.role.assign` on the organization, for a project binding as well, and every permission of the role at the binding's scope: a permission held on the organization counts for any scope, one held on a project only for that project. Refused with `NOT_FOUND` when no account has `--member`'s address as its verified email: nothing is held for an address until its account exists. Refused with `CONFLICT` when the member already holds the role at that scope, and with `BAD_REQUEST` when the member is a deleted service account.

```sh
origin iam create-role-binding [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --member <MEMBER> --role <ROLE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--member <MEMBER>` | yes | Who holds the role: `user:{email}` or `serviceAccount:{service_account}`. A user is shown with their account's current verified address, as `userId:{user}` when it has none, or as `deleted:user:{user}` once the account is gone. |
| `--role <ROLE>` | yes | The role granted, `roles/{role}`. Its id, or its whole name, `roles/{role}`. |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project the binding is limited to, `projects/{project}`, one of the organization's. Empty for a binding on the whole organization, which covers every project in it. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day returns the binding the first request created, as it is now, instead of being refused as a conflict. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-role-binding

Removes a role binding. Needs `iam.role.revoke` on the organization and every permission of the role at the binding's scope, as CreateRoleBinding does. Refused with `CONFLICT`, removing nothing, when it is the organization's last organization-wide binding of `roles/owner`: bind another owner first.

```sh
origin iam delete-role-binding [OPTIONS] --role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--role-binding` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>` | yes | The binding to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day succeeds as the first did, instead of answering `NOT_FOUND`. One is generated when not given. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-service-account

Returns a service account, deleted or not. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-service-account [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |

### list-service-accounts

Lists an organization's service accounts, oldest first. Deleted ones are listed only when `--show-deleted` is set. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-service-accounts [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most service accounts to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--show-deleted <true|false>` | no | Whether deleted service accounts are listed too. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |

### create-service-account

Creates a service account and, for an `EXTERNAL` one, its client secret, which expires after `--secret-lifetime`. The response is the only place the secret is ever shown: store it now. Needs `iam.service_account.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam create-service-account [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | A name of your own, shown in the console; at most 100 characters. |
| `--type <TYPE>` | no | How the service account authenticates; `EXTERNAL` when the create leaves it unset. Possible values: `EXTERNAL`, `WORKLOAD`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day creates nothing and is refused with `CONFLICT`: the secret went to the first request only. The error's `ErrorInfo` metadata names the service account under `serviceAccount`; delete it and create a new one to get a working secret. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT` without that metadata. One is generated when not given. |
| `--secret-lifetime <DURATION>` | no | How long an `EXTERNAL` service account's client secret is accepted, from its creation: more than zero and at most 365 days. 90 days when left out. A `WORKLOAD` service account has no secret, and a create of one that sets it is refused. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |

### rotate-service-account-secret

Issues a new client secret for an `EXTERNAL` service account and returns the service account with it in `clientSecret`, the only place it is ever shown. The previous secret is refused from then on, and the new one is accepted at once, also when the previous one had expired. It expires after `--secret-lifetime`. An access token issued before stays valid until it expires, within minutes. Needs `iam.service_account.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam rotate-service-account-secret [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The `EXTERNAL` service account whose secret to replace. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--secret-lifetime <DURATION>` | no | How long the new secret is accepted, from now: more than zero and at most 365 days. 90 days when left out. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day issues no secret and is refused with `CONFLICT`: the secret went to the first request only. Rotate again with a new `--request-id` to get a working secret. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT` too. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-service-account

Deletes a service account for good: its credential is refused from then on, an access token it already holds is refused on its next request, and every role binding it holds, in any organization, is removed. It stays readable as `DELETED`. Deleting a deleted service account succeeds. Needs `iam.service_account.revoke` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam delete-service-account [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-user

Returns the caller's own profile. Any other user is `NOT_FOUND`; a service account caller is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`, having no profile.

```sh
origin iam get-user [OPTIONS] --user <USER>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--user <USER>` | yes | The user to return: `users/me`, or the caller's own `users/{user}`. Its id, or its whole name, `users/{user}`. |

## origin sts

The security token service: it turns a token from an identity provider outside Origin Cloud, such as a CI job's OIDC token, into the access token of a `WORKLOAD` service account that trusts it through a federated credential. It authenticates no caller: the token is the proof.

Every `origin sts` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://sts.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_STS_ENDPOINT`. |

### assume-service-account

Assumes a `WORKLOAD` service account with an OIDC token. Exactly one federated credential, of the named service account or of any, must trust the token: its issuer and audience, and every one of its conditions. The token is verified with its issuer's published keys (RS256), and a pull request's job is admitted only by a credential that names its `event_name`. Refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` when the token isn't trusted, without saying why, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when its issuer or the trust can't be read now.

```sh
origin sts assume-service-account [OPTIONS] --oidc-token-file <PATH>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The `{organization}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--oidc-token-file <PATH>` | yes | The OIDC token, a JWT its issuer signed, such as a CI job's. Read from the file at the path, or from standard input with `-`, without its final newline. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account to assume, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Only its federated credentials are considered. Without it, any service account's credential that trusts the token is. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its whole name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--lifetime <DURATION>` | no | How long the access token lives: from 60 seconds to 1 hour, 15 minutes when unset. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |
